### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **7** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/driver-memory`, `@objectstack/driver-mongodb`, `@objectstack/driver-sql`, `@objectstack/driver-sqlite-wasm`, `@objectstack/driver-turso`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **79** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**45** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1ced0f82bd93260b660e6f448c7dc5952bc82371`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `organization_id (symbol, 33 pages)`
- **14** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **150** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1ced0f82bd93260b660e6f448c7dc5952bc82371` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2489c7f91b523c0c307d969fca32921c2c7acd07` — the merge of head `45a871de4d1735f9c4bbaa5855f87c4c3039a023` into base `1ced0f82bd93260b660e6f448c7dc5952bc82371`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2489c7f91b523c0c307d969fca32921c2c7acd07 && git checkout 2489c7f91b523c0c307d969fca32921c2c7acd07
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1ced0f82bd93260b660e6f448c7dc5952bc82371 45a871de4d1735f9c4bbaa5855f87c4c3039a023 && git checkout -B drift-repro 1ced0f82bd93260b660e6f448c7dc5952bc82371 && git merge --no-ff 45a871de4d1735f9c4bbaa5855f87c4c3039a023

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1ced0f82bd93260b660e6f448c7dc5952bc82371
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 1ced0f82bd93260b660e6f448c7dc5952bc82371` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `45a871de4d1735f9c4bbaa5855f87c4c3039a023`
Local-runs: none

Reviewed on the card (#23639, body and every comment), the PR body, its 21-file list, the net diff against `main` at the head, and the head's 39 check-runs. Governing text: ADR-0139 D1 to D3 and plan rows E3/E4; ADR-0112 (the envelope); #22788 note 3 (ruling pointer 6104842076: D3 stands as written, no capability bit, mongodb refuses until O3); the `domain:spec` ruling 6137585321 (the case-set lands in the same PR as the five suites, zero ledger rows); the #5499 freeze on `driver-memory` / `driver-mongodb`. Tier basis: `packages/spec/src/data/index.ts` is a published schema surface (schema face). No path in the file list is a governed-register row; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is green.

### ① Derived judgments

**Public surface, `@objectstack/spec/data` — widens by six consts and five types** (`READABLE_IDS_CASES`, `READABLE_IDS_PARENT_OBJECT`, `READABLE_IDS_CHILD_OBJECT`, `READABLE_IDS_PARENT_ROWS`, `READABLE_IDS_CHILD_ROWS`, `READABLE_IDS_REFUSAL`; `ReadableIdsCase`, `ReadableIdsMatchesCase`, `ReadableIdsRefusesUncomposedCase`, `ReadableIdsParentRow`, `ReadableIdsChildRow`). **Right.** Ruled by 6137585321 and declared cross-lane in the claim. `api-surface/data.json` and `export-origins/data.json` name exactly those eleven and nothing else. The carried file, its oracle test and the `CASE_SETS` row were diffed against the parked `e641ab6d8`: byte-identical except the one declared doc-link edit (`readableIdsCaseHoldsComposedLeaf`, a symbol that never existed, now `ReadableIdsMatchesCase.holdsComposedLeaf`). The gate's `CASE_SETS_DIR` is `packages/spec/src/data`, so the file sits where the other nine case-sets sit; it holds fixtures, a frozen envelope constant and `where` factories, no runtime logic (Prime Directive 2 holds).

**Public surface, `@objectstack/core` — widens by four functions and three types** (`findMisplacedReadableIds`, `replaceComposedReadableIds`, `readableIdsDriverRefusal`, `refuseReadableIdsOnce`; `MisplacedReadableIds`, `ReadableIdsDriverRefusalError`, `ReadableIdsRefusalLog`). **Right.** Outside the claim's original surface, accepted into it by the seat's amendment on the dev's report (claim 6187884851, amended). The precedent is exact: `json-column-operator-refusal.ts` sits on the same floor for the same reason, four compilers that do not import each other. Core carries no api-surface artifact, so nothing was owed there. Covered by the changeset's core row.

**`driver-sql` accept-set.** (a) A composed leaf as a `$in` comparand compiles to `field IN (SELECT id FROM P_TABLE WHERE SCOPE AND TENANT)`: **right per D3.** The wall is `applyTenantScope` on the parent with the outer read's options, threaded as a new optional trailing `options` on the protected `applyFilters` and `applyFilterCondition`. Verified at the head: all eight in-file `applyFilters` call sites pass the options they already hand `applyTenantScope`; no in-tree subclass overrides either method, so nothing can drop them; `compileFilters` keys the scope's compile off the sub-builder's table (`coercionKey`), so the scope compiles against the parent's own declarations; `getBuilder(parent)` without options omits only a transaction binding, which an embedded subquery never needs; `check:tenant-chokepoint` (inside the green `Lint & Repo Gates`) accepts the new builder because it does call the chokepoint. (b) An uncomposed leaf at any position, or a composed leaf outside a `$in` comparand, is refused `INTERNAL_ERROR` / 500 before anything compiles, ahead of the withheld-refusal resolver: **right** (D2's last paragraph, D3); it replaces the `DATABASE_ERROR` syntax fault E1's pointer (6107554336) measured. (c) The composed arm binds the bare `field`, exactly as the list `$in` arm does: consistent. (d) New protected members `readableIdsRefusalLog`, `readableIdsDriverName`, `readableIdsSubquery`: a subclassing-surface widening, minor. (e) The compile runs wherever `applyFilters` runs, the update/delete predicates included: **right**; the driver is below D1's seam, which refuses the leaf on write verbs, and a driver is not that seam.

**`driver-sqlite-wasm`, `driver-turso` local face — inherit.** **Right.** Each overrides only the name its refusal prints; each is measured by its own suite on its own engine rather than assumed from the inheritance.

**`driver-turso` remote face.** `TursoDriver#toRemoteWhere` refuses first (same walk, logged once per instance), then resolves each composed leaf into a branded `RemoteReadableIdsSemiJoin` (the parent's remote table; the scope in storage form via `toRemoteFilter` on the parent; the tenant wall via `remoteTenantScope`, which compiles what `applyTenantScope` adds with the outer read's options). `RemoteTransport`'s `$in` arm compiles `column IN (SELECT "id" FROM table WHERE (scope) AND (tenant))`, binding only the scope's and the wall's values; a composed leaf the driver did not resolve (the transport driven standalone) is refused `unsupported`; `buildWhereSQL` refuses uncomposed and misplaced leaves at its outermost frame. **Right per D3** (an independent compiler, the same compilation, the wall decided in one place). `find`, `findOne`, `count`, `aggregate`, `distinct`, `updateMany` and `deleteMany` all thread options into `toRemoteQuery`. The brand and its factory are module exports, but `driver-turso`'s `index.ts` exports named symbols only, so the package's public surface does not widen by them.

**`driver-memory`.** `convertToMongoQuery`, the one funnel for `find`, `count`, `aggregate` and `distinct`, refuses first, then rewrites each composed leaf copy-on-write into the parent's ids read under the scope through the same funnel, ahead of the shape gate. **Right per D3** (in process, unbounded; no wall owed, because `assertSingleTenantPosture` refuses every tenant-scoped call, and the tenant-wall case records that refusal instead of rows, as the case-set prescribes). Replaces the raw `TypeError` E1's pointer measured. The package diff is +32/-2 and nothing but the D3 row rides: the #5499 freeze is respected.

**`driver-mongodb`.** `translateFilter` refuses every leaf, composed or not, ahead of the shape gate that would otherwise answer `INVALID_FILTER`. **Right per D3 and note 3.** Every door and the aggregation `$match` funnel through it, and the suite pins the pipeline path. The package diff is +20/-0: the freeze is respected.

**The envelope.** One helper, `code: 'INTERNAL_ERROR'`, `status: 500`, `httpStatus: 500`, a message naming the driver, the leaf's path and parent object, and the remedy; three kinds (`uncomposed`, `misplaced`, `unsupported`). **Right** (ADR-0112: `httpStatus` is the target location, `status` keeps the server-fault declaration true; never `INVALID_FILTER`; the `unsupported` remedy names the probe chosen before the leaf is written, D5's rule, never a catch). No `DriverCapabilities` bit anywhere in the diff. Runtime strings carry no tracker number (`check:doc-authoring` green).

**Logging.** `error` once per driver instance on SQL, Turso and memory through each driver's own logger; the sink contract falls back to `warn` only where a host injects a logger with no `error`, the contract `SqlDriver.logger` already documents, and the head's last commit makes `warn` required so the line is never dropped. **Right.**

**Conformance.** Five suites import `READABLE_IDS_CASES` from `@objectstack/spec/data` (no hand copy) and run every case through `lowerFilterCondition`, the seam a real read passes; the lowering spreads nodes and arrays but never a non-array comparand, so the composed leaf keeps its brand by reference, which the NULL-safe `$not` case depends on. E3's pins hold on the sqlite cell, Turso remote and memory: over 2,000 readable candidates served in full, an unreadable row hidden, a deleted parent excluded on find, count and aggregate, `count` equal to rows served; the O1 reading captures at most 3 bindings whatever the parent's size. `check:driver-conformance` (in the green `Lint & Repo Gates`) accepts the classified set with zero ledger rows, so E4's "the table records both" holds without DEBT.

**Residuals, named, none a breach.** (a) The PG and MySQL cells of the new `driver-sql` suite are named skips on the PR fast set and first execute on `main`'s full battery (`Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` runs the whole `driver-sql` suite with both URLs and `OS_EXPECT_LIVE_DIALECT_MATRIX=1`); the form is a plain `IN (SELECT …)` through knex's per-dialect compiler, and a red there is the lane's main-red by the standing convention. (b) O1: SQLite measured (32,766 accepted, 32,767 refused); Postgres and MySQL honestly `NOT MEASURED`, documented 65,535; the statement binds no per-id parameter, so the ceiling moves into the scope exactly as the record's consequences say. (c) The PR body's verification record names `52dc068bfc`; the head adds one commit that only tightens the sink contract in core (`warn` required). The diff judged here is the net diff at the head.

**Check-runs on the head.** Green: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `Type Check · source gates`, every `Lint ·` job, `Spec property liveness`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, the issue-claim, single-writer, part-of and branch-claim guards. Skipped by design (full-battery or opt-in): `Build Docs`, `Console Pin Gate`, the three dogfood shards, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Packed-tarball smoke`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`. **Pending, not a verdict this record renders:** `Build Core`; `Test Core` 1/6 through 6/6; `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Type Check · workspace`. The owning seat lands only once every required context concludes `success`.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/23639-readable-ids-drivers.md`: seven packages at `minor` (`@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/driver-sql`, `@objectstack/driver-sqlite-wasm`, `@objectstack/driver-turso`, `@objectstack/driver-memory`, `@objectstack/driver-mongodb`). **Matches what the diff publishes.** Spec and core publish new exports, a widening, so at least minor. Each of the five drivers gains a new compiled form or a new refusal envelope on an input that previously produced an undeclared fault (a `DATABASE_ERROR` syntax fault, a raw `TypeError`, a pass-through): a capability, not a fix, so minor and not patch. `driver-sqlite-wasm`'s own diff is a two-line name override, but it ships the compile through the inherited compiler and minor is the honest level for what it now does. Nothing removes or renames anything an author can write or a consumer imports; the optional trailing parameter on two protected methods is compatible; so not breaking, no ADR-0087 disposition owed, no migration text owed. `skip-changeset` would be wrong and is not used. `Check Changeset` is green on the head.

`Clause-②: yes` with no arm, on the PR body and the changeset body alike. **Right:** `yes` takes at least minor, which every row carries; `(narrowing)` would be false and `(widening)` is not asserted, so the pair is well-formed. The card's claim declared `Clause-②: yes` for the spec half; the core export line falls inside the same `yes` by the seat's amendment.

### ③ Boundary flags

Every dev flag answered; nothing escalated.

- **open_questions[0] — the shared walk, rewrite and refusal live in `@objectstack/core`, outside the claim's surface.** Option A, keep it in core: **accepted** (the seat already amended the claim; this record concurs). One source for four compilers that do not import each other, on the floor `json-column-operator-refusal.ts` already proves; four hand copies is how one refusal becomes four dialects.
- **open_questions[1] — mongodb's once-per-driver line goes to `console.error` once per process.** Option A: **accepted.** Verified at the head: `mongodb-driver.ts` carries no logger of any kind, and the refusal is raised in the pure `translateFilter` that every door and the aggregation `$match` share, so one site covers all. Option B widens a driver #5499 freezes. Once per process is once per driver package, and every refusal still reaches the caller. Recorded in the PR's acceptance notes; not escalated.
- **open_questions[2] — the Turso remote face resolves the leaf on `updateMany` / `deleteMany` too.** Option A: **right.** The local face compiles wherever `applyFilters` runs; keeping the two faces of one driver identical is the contract. The write-verb refusal is D1's, at the engine, and no driver is its enforcement point.
- **open_questions[3] — `minor` for the five drivers.** **Stands** (see ②). The seat does not lower it.
- **open_questions[4] — role file over harness defaults (no CI wait, session-URL footer, model-free commit trailers, the primary checkout detached and restored).** No contract content. The PR body does end with the session-URL footer. No action.
- **deviations — the core file, its test and the `index.ts` export line; the two-line `readableIdsDriverName` override in `driver-sqlite-wasm`; `turso-driver.ts` (`toRemoteWhere`).** All three named in the seat's amended file surface; all three judged above. **Closed.**
- **deviations — the one doc-link edit to the carried case-set.** Verified as the sole difference against `e641ab6d8`. **Right**, because this PR is the one that lands the file.
- **out_of_scope_findings — none filed.** Right: the two environment notes (a full-repo dist for `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, a missing objectql `.d.ts` locally) are not reproducible defects, contract violations or authoring traps; CI covers the first.
- **Readings the card owes.** O1 answered (above, with the honest `NOT MEASURED` for the two server dialects); O3 kept (mongodb refuses, no prototype); the conformance ledger read before and after by the dev and re-derived by the green gate on this head: zero new DEBT rows.
